Regulation: B.C. Reg. 153/2026
Made under: Safe Access To Schools Act
Published in: No. 16 – B.C. Regs. 153 to 162, September 22, including September 8, 2026
Deposit date: September 8, 2026

B.C. Reg. 153/2026, deposited September 8, 2026, under theSAFE ACCESS TO SCHOOLS ACT[sections 3 and 8]. Order in Council 394/2026, approved and ordered September 8, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that the attached Safe Access to Schools Regulation is made. — L. BEARE,Minister of Education and Child Care; R. PARMAR,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. SAFE ACCESS TO SCHOOLS REGULATION 1In this regulation,"Act"means theSafe Access to Schools Act. 2Access zones are established for the following schools: (a)	schools operated by a board of education, other than the Qwam Qwum Stuwixwulh Community School in the City of Nanaimo; (b)	schools operated by a francophone education authority; (c)	schools operated by an independent school authority, other than the schools set out in column 2 of the Schedule to this regulation. 3For the purposes of the definition of "police officer" in section 1 of the Act, the designated policing unit known as the Stl’atl’imx Tribal Police Service is prescribed. Chief and Councillors of the Kitsumkalum Indian Band Chief and Councillors of the Fort Ware Indian Band Nuxalk Acwsalcmalslayc Academy of Learning Society Bella Bella Community School Society Chalo Independent School Society Chief and Councillors of the Lower Nicola Indian Band Chief and Councillors of the Iskut Band Łuwechon Kots'ede'i Kime School The Ahousat Education Authority The Ahousat Education Authority

minutes_briefs.title: BC creates protected access zones around most schools under new Safe Access to Schools Regulation
minutes_briefs.summary: BC has made a new regulation under the Safe Access to Schools Act that sets up access zones (protected areas around school property where certain activities can be restricted) for most schools in the province. The zones cover public schools run by boards of education, francophone schools, and most independent schools, with a few named exceptions such as the Qwam Qwum Stuwixwulh Community School in Nanaimo and the independent schools listed in the regulation's schedule. The regulation also names the Stl'atl'imx Tribal Police Service as a police officer for the purposes of the Act.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Check whether your school is covered by the new access zones and brief staff and visitors on what is now restricted near school property.
